lead_headline: Subscriptions jump +2 net as restaurant leads hold near 270 and liquor filings stay frozen for week four

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today: Good Practice pay-what-you-can art cafe (Jefferson Park), Sherpa Base Camp (Uptown), Dairy Queen closure (Fort Logan). Active leads: 268.

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications again — the complete freeze now extends to four full weeks with no new bar, restaurant, or retail license filings across the 12,325-license database. Previous summer lulls rarely exceeded 10 days. This represents the longest application drought in the tracker's history, raising questions about whether July 4 holiday timing, economic headwinds, or regulatory backlogs are suppressing new hospitality ventures. The last application logged was early June.

reputation.blurb: 5 mentions yesterday — social chatter on Reddit and Facebook dominated coverage, while dasbluebird.de picked up the Fluid Truck bankruptcy story. The 7-day total jumped to 70 mentions across 14 sources, up from 52 the prior week (+35% week-over-week). Facebook leads with 20 pickups, followed by Reddit (16) and Instagram (8). The Denver Post contributed 6 pieces. Primary election coverage and Uptown shelter permitting drove engagement, while the Fluid Truck $35M debt reveal got international pickup.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 yesterday (2 new, 0 canceled) lifts MTD to +5 — the month opened slowly but gained momentum Monday-Tuesday. 90-day net stands at +132. The past seven days delivered +23 net (40 new, 17 canceled), a sharp reversal from the prior week's flat performance (10 new, 10 canceled). Sunday-Monday produced a +16 two-day surge, the strongest 48-hour stretch since mid-June. The recent acceleration contrasts with late June's stagnation, restoring the steady YTD pace of +1.3/day.
